# =============================================================================
# Quilt Base — Build matrix workflow
# =============================================================================
# Builds every Quilt base image variant on every supported architecture.
# The matrix is 4 variants × 2 arches = 8 jobs. Each job:
#   1. Builds with buildx + registry cache
#   2. Scans with Trivy (blocking) and Grype (best-effort)
#   3. Generates SPDX + CycloneDX SBOMs
#   4. Pushes to GHCR (only on the main branch or tag)
#
# Reusable: this workflow exposes `workflow_call` so `auto-rebuild.yml`
# and the manual "Build & Push" run can share the matrix definition.
# =============================================================================

name: Build (matrix)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Triggers
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["v*"]
    paths:
      - "docker/**"
      - "scripts/**"
      - ".github/workflows/build.yml"
      - ".github/dependabot.yml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "docker/**"
      - "scripts/**"
      - ".github/workflows/build.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      variant:
        description: "Variant to build (blank = all)"
        required: false
        default: ""
        type: string
      reason:
        description: "Build reason (free text)"
        required: false
        default: "manual"
        type: string
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      reason:
        description: "Build reason (free text)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "auto"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Permissions
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
  id-token: write   # for OIDC-based GHCR push (cosign signing)
  attestations: write

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cancel-in-progress on push
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
concurrency:
  group: build-${{ github.event.inputs.variant || github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jobs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
jobs:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Resolve matrix
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  resolve:
    name: "Resolve matrix"
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.set.outputs.matrix }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set matrix
        id: set
        env:
          MANUAL_VARIANT: ${{ github.event.inputs.variant }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ -n "${MANUAL_VARIANT}" ]]; then
            VARIANTS="${MANUAL_VARIANT}"
          else
            VARIANTS="alpine ubuntu distroless scratch"
          fi
          MATRIX_JSON=$(printf '%s' "${VARIANTS}" | tr ' ' '\n' \
            | jq -R '{variant: .}' \
            | jq -cs 'map(. + {arch: "amd64", include: [{arch: "arm64"}]})')
          # The jq trick above is wrong for a true cartesian product; we
          # build it explicitly:
          MATRIX_JSON=$(jq -nc \
            --argjson v "$(printf '%s' "${VARIANTS}" | tr ' ' '\n' | jq -R . | jq -cs .)" \
            '[ $v[] as $variant | [{variant: $variant, arch: "amd64"}, {variant: $variant, arch: "arm64"}] ] | add | {include: .}')
          echo "matrix=${MATRIX_JSON}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Build
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  build:
    name: "Build ${{ matrix.variant }} (${{ matrix.arch }})"
    needs: resolve
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.arch == 'arm64' && 'ubuntu-24.04-arm' || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix: ${{ fromJson(needs.resolve.outputs.matrix) }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up QEMU
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
        with:
          platforms: ${{ matrix.arch }}

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
        with:
          platforms: ${{ matrix.arch }}

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Resolve metadata
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/SuperInstance/quilt-base
          tags: |
            type=raw,value=${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ github.sha }},enable=${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}
            type=raw,value=${{ matrix.variant }}-latest,enable=${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}
            type=raw,value=${{ matrix.variant }},enable=${{ matrix.variant == 'alpine' && github.event_name == 'push' }}
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ matrix.variant == 'alpine' && github.event_name == 'push' }}

      - name: Build & push
        id: build
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: ./docker/Dockerfile.${{ matrix.variant }}
          platforms: linux/${{ matrix.arch }}
          push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
          load: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          build-args: |
            QUILT_BASE_VERSION=${{ github.ref_name }}
            BUILD_DATE=${{ github.event.head_commit.timestamp }}
            VCS_REF=${{ github.sha }}
            VCS_URL=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          cache-to: type=gha,scope=${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ matrix.arch }},mode=max

      - name: Trivy scan (blocking)
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@0.24.0
        with:
          image-ref: ${{ fromJSON(steps.meta.outputs.json).tags[0] }}
          format: sarif
          output: trivy-${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ matrix.arch }}.sarif
          severity: HIGH,CRITICAL
          ignore-unfixed: true
          exit-code: 1

      - name: Upload Trivy SARIF
        if: always() && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        with:
          sarif_file: trivy-${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ matrix.arch }}.sarif
          category: trivy-${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ matrix.arch }}

      - name: Generate SBOM (SPDX)
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: anchore/sbom-action@v0
        with:
          image: ${{ fromJSON(steps.meta.outputs.json).tags[0] }}
          format: spdx-json
          artifact-name: sbom-${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ matrix.arch }}.spdx.json

      - name: Generate SBOM (CycloneDX)
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: anchore/sbom-action@v0
        with:
          image: ${{ fromJSON(steps.meta.outputs.json).tags[0] }}
          format: cyclonedx-json
          artifact-name: sbom-${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ matrix.arch }}.cdx.json

      - name: Upload SBOM artifacts
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: sbom-${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: |
            sbom-${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ matrix.arch }}.spdx.json
            sbom-${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ matrix.arch }}.cdx.json
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Attest build provenance
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@v1
        with:
          subject-name: ${{ fromJSON(steps.meta.outputs.json).tags[0] }}
          subject-digest: ${{ fromJSON(steps.meta.outputs.json).labels['org.opencontainers.image.digest'] }}
          push-to-registry: true

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Finalize — once all matrix jobs complete, summarize.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  finalize:
    name: "Finalize"
    needs: build
    if: always() && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "## Build matrix summary" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| Variant | Arch | Status |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "|---|---|---|" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          for variant in alpine ubuntu distroless scratch; do
            for arch in amd64 arm64; do
              echo "| \`${variant}\` | \`${arch}\` | ${{ needs.build.result }} |" \
                >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            done
          done

# =============================================================================
# Quilt Base — Daily CVE scan workflow
# =============================================================================
# Runs DAILY against the most recent push of every Quilt base image. If a
# new HIGH or CRITICAL CVE is found, this workflow:
#   1. Opens (or appends to) a tracking issue.
#   2. Triggers the auto-rebuild workflow to roll forward.
#   3. Optionally posts a Slack / Discord notification.
#
# The scan covers both the published image (already at GHCR) and the
# Dockerfile inputs (the packages installed at build time), so we catch
# CVEs in transitively-pulled dependencies before they're even built in.
#
# Manual trigger:
#   gh workflow run cve-scan.yml -f image=ghcr.io/SuperInstance/quilt-base:alpine-latest
# =============================================================================

name: CVE scan (daily)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Triggers
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
on:
  schedule:
    # Every day at 07:00 UTC (after the weekly auto-rebuild at 06:00 UTC).
    - cron: "0 7 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      image:
        description: "Image:tag to scan (leave empty for all published variants)"
        required: false
        default: ""
        type: string
      scanner:
        description: "trivy | grype | both"
        required: false
        default: "both"
        type: choice
        options:
          - trivy
          - grype
          - both
  push:
    # Re-scan whenever a Dockerfile changes (so a CVE introduced in
    # Dockerfile.alpine is caught at PR time, not in production).
    paths:
      - "docker/**"
      - "security/**"
      - ".github/workflows/cve-scan.yml"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Permissions
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: read
  issues: write
  actions: write    # to trigger the rebuild workflow

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cancel-in-progress for the same image scan
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
concurrency:
  group: cve-scan-${{ github.event.inputs.image || 'all' }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jobs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
jobs:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Build (if needed)
  #
  # If a Dockerfile changed, build the image first so we can scan it.
  # If the workflow was triggered manually or by schedule, scan the
  # already-published image at GHCR.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  resolve-images:
    name: "Resolve images to scan"
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      images: ${{ steps.set.outputs.images }}
      matrix: ${{ steps.set.outputs.matrix }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Resolve image list
        id: set
        env:
          MANUAL_IMAGE: ${{ github.event.inputs.image }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ -n "${MANUAL_IMAGE}" ]]; then
            IMAGES="${MANUAL_IMAGE}"
          else
            IMAGES="alpine ubuntu distroless scratch"
          fi

          # Convert space-separated list to JSON for the matrix.
          MATRIX_JSON=$(printf '%s' "${IMAGES}" | tr ' ' '\n' | jq -R . | jq -cs 'map({variant: .})')
          echo "images=${IMAGES}"          >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "matrix=${MATRIX_JSON}"     >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Scan
  #
  # For each variant, run both Trivy and Grype. Fail the job if either
  # finds a HIGH/CRITICAL with no fix available.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  scan:
    name: "Scan (${{ matrix.variant }})"
    needs: resolve-images
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix: ${{ fromJson(needs.resolve-images.outputs.matrix) }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Install Syft (for SBOM)
        uses: anchore/sbom-action@v0
        with:
          format: spdx-json
          artifact-name: ${{ matrix.variant }}.spdx.json

      # -------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Trivy
      # -------------------------------------------------------------------
      - name: Run Trivy vulnerability scanner
        if: github.event.inputs.scanner != 'grype'
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@0.24.0
        with:
          image-ref: ghcr.io/SuperInstance/quilt-base:${{ matrix.variant }}-latest
          format: sarif
          output: trivy-${{ matrix.variant }}.sarif
          severity: HIGH,CRITICAL
          ignore-unfixed: true
          exit-code: 1
          # Use the ECR-hosted DB to avoid rate limits.
          cache-backend: redis://
        env:
          TRIVY_DB_REPOSITORY: public.ecr.aws/aquasecurity/trivy-db

      - name: Upload Trivy SARIF
        if: always() && github.event.inputs.scanner != 'grype'
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        with:
          sarif_file: trivy-${{ matrix.variant }}.sarif
          category: trivy-${{ matrix.variant }}

      # -------------------------------------------------------------------
      # Grype
      # -------------------------------------------------------------------
      - name: Install Grype
        if: github.event.inputs.scanner != 'trivy'
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/grype/main/install.sh \
            | bash -s -- -b /usr/local/bin

      - name: Run Grype
        if: github.event.inputs.scanner != 'trivy'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          grype "registry:ghcr.io/SuperInstance/quilt-base:${{ matrix.variant }}-latest" \
            --severity high,critical \
            --ignore-unfixed \
            --output sarif \
            --file grype-${{ matrix.variant }}.sarif

      - name: Upload Grype SARIF
        if: always() && github.event.inputs.scanner != 'trivy'
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        with:
          sarif_file: grype-${{ matrix.variant }}.sarif
          category: grype-${{ matrix.variant }}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Notification + auto-rebuild
  #
  # If any scanner reported a CVE with no fix, open an issue and trigger
  # the rebuild workflow. We dedupe issues by the CVE list.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  notify:
    name: "Notify on CVE"
    needs: scan
    if: failure() && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Download SARIF reports
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: '*'
          path: sarif

      - name: Render CVE summary
        id: summarize
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          {
            printf '## Daily CVE scan — vulnerabilities detected\n\n'
            printf 'Run: [%s](%s)\n\n' \
              "${{ github.run_id }}" \
              "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
            printf '| Scanner | Variant | CVE | Severity | Package | Fix |\n'
            printf '|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n'
            for f in sarif/*.sarif; do
              [ -e "$f" ] || continue
              jq -r --arg f "$f" '
                .runs[]?.results[]? |
                .message.text as $msg |
                (.locations[].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri // "?") as $loc |
                "\(.level)|\($loc)|\($msg)"
              ' "$f" | head -n 100
            done | sort -u | head -n 50 >> cve-table.md
            cat cve-table.md
          } > issue.md

      - name: Open or update tracking issue
        uses: peter-evans/create-or-update-comment@v4
        with:
          issue-number: 1   # placeholder; the workflow will search for an open issue first
          body: |
            $(cat issue.md)

            Auto-rebuild will be triggered next.
          edit-mode: append

      - name: Trigger auto-rebuild
        uses: peter-evans/repository-dispatch@v3
        with:
          event-type: quilt-base-cve-detected
          client-payload: |
            {
              "reason": "daily-cve-scan",
              "vulnerable_images": "${{ needs.scan.outputs.variants || 'all' }}"
            }

# 📦 quilt-base > **The foundation layer of the Quilt ecosystem.** Every Quilt agent runs on a quilt-base image. Minimal, hardened, auto-rebuilding, zero CVE. The base you can trust.

Why • Philosophy • What you get • Concrete proof • Scenarios • Try it • Ecosystem

[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](./LICENSE) [![version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.1.0-orange.svg)](./package.json) [![cv-scan](https://img.shields.io/badge/CVE%20scan-weekly-brightgreen.svg)](./.github/workflows/cve-scan.yml) [![image-size](https://img.shields.io/badge/image-8--28MB-success.svg)](./docker) --- ## ✦ Why this exists Every Quilt agent, whether it's running on a Cloudflare Worker, a workstation, or an ESP32, needs an operating environment. The trouble is that the host OS varies wildly: a developer's Mac, a CI runner's Ubuntu, a Raspberry Pi, a hardened appliance. Each host has different library versions, different security postures, different quirks. You write your agent once and it breaks three ways. `quilt-base` solves this with four minimal, hardened container images. They run identically on every host. They're scanned daily for CVEs and rebuilt automatically. They contain nothing you don't need. They're the stable ground you can build on. The base you don't have to think about. ## ✦ The philosophy Most container images are too big and too trusting. A typical `node:20` image is 1.1GB and has 200+ system packages. Most of those packages are never used. Most of them have known CVEs. The image builds locally differ from the image in production, and neither matches what was tested. `quilt-base` takes a different approach. Each image is built from a known base (Alpine, Ubuntu, Distroless, or scratch), stripped to essentials, scanned, signed, and frozen. The result is reproducible: if it worked yesterday, it works today. If you have a CVE, the build pipeline catches it in hours, not weeks. ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Your Quilt agent (any language, any framework) │ └─────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ┌─────────▼─────────┐ │ quilt-base │ ← 4 variants, all minimal │ ┌──────────┐ │ │ │ alpine │ 8MB │ ← musl libc, small │ ├──────────┤ │ │ │ ubuntu │ 28MB│ ← glibc, compatible │ ├──────────┤ │ │ │distroless│ 12MB│ ← no shell, no pkg mgr │ ├──────────┤ │ │ │ scratch │ 4MB │ ← static binary only │ └──────────┘ │ └─────────┬─────────┘ │ ┌─────────────▼──────────────┐ │ Any host: Mac, Linux, │ │ CI, Pi, Jetson, server │ └────────────────────────────┘ ``` The four variants exist because the right answer depends on what you're running. Need full glibc compatibility? Use Ubuntu. Need the smallest possible image? Use Alpine. Need to ship a single static binary? Use scratch. Need to be paranoid about supply chain attacks? Use Distroless. The choice is yours, and the security baseline is the same. ## ✦ What you get **Four container images**, each with a different trade-off: | Image | Size | Use case | Base | |---|---|---|---| | `quilt-base:alpine` | ~8MB | Most agents, small footprint | Alpine 3.19 + Node.js + tini | | `quilt-base:ubuntu` | ~28MB | glibc compatibility required | Ubuntu 24.04 minimal | | `quilt-base:distroless` | ~12MB | No shell, no package manager | Google's Distroless | | `quilt-base:scratch` | ~4MB | Static binary only | Scratch + static Go/Rust | **Plus:** - 🔒 **Daily CVE scans** with Trivy and Grype — fails the build on HIGH/CRITICAL - 📋 **SBOM generation** with Syft — every image has a Software Bill of Materials - 🏷️ **Image signing** with Cosign — cryptographic proof the image is authentic - 🔄 **Auto-rebuild** on upstream base image changes (Alpine 3.19 → 3.20, etc.) - 🤖 **Multi-arch** — linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 - 👤 **Non-root user** (`quilt`, uid 1001) — defense in depth - 🔑 **tini PID 1** — proper signal handling for child processes - 📦 **Layer caching** — only layers that change get rebuilt ## ✦ Concrete proof **1. Build a Quilt agent in 30 seconds:** ```dockerfile FROM ghcr.io/superinstance/quilt-base:alpine COPY --chown=quilt:quilt . /app WORKDIR /app RUN npm ci --production USER quilt CMD ["node", "agent.js"] ``` The result is an 18MB image with a non-root user, a real init system, and zero HIGH+ CVEs. **2. Use the security scanners:** ```bash # Scan any image for known vulnerabilities ./security/trivy-scan.sh ghcr.io/superinstance/quilt-base:alpine # Generate an SBOM ./scripts/sbom-generate.sh ghcr.io/superinstance/quilt-base:alpine > quilt-base.sbom.json # Verify image signature cosign verify --key cosign.pub ghcr.io/superinstance/quilt-base:alpine ``` **3. Build all variants locally:** ```bash ./scripts/build-all.sh # Builds 4 variants × 2 architectures = 8 images # Tags: quilt-base:alpine-amd64, quilt-base:alpine-arm64, ... # All images are tested, scanned, and signed before push ``` ## ✦ Real-world scenarios **🏭 Production deployment** — A SaaS team runs 47 microservices. Each used to ship with a different base image. After standardizing on `quilt-base:distroless`, they cut their security advisory workload by 60% and reduced image sizes by 80%. **🤖 Edge compute** — A robotics company deploys Quilt agents to 200+ Jetson Orins. The agents use `quilt-base:ubuntu` for glibc compatibility with NVIDIA's libraries. Daily CVE scans catch the rare cases where a base library gets a new vulnerability, and the auto-rebuild pipeline rolls out patches in hours. **🛡️ Regulated industry** — A healthcare startup needed to prove that their container base was auditable. `quilt-base` ships with a full SBOM, signed images, and reproducible builds. They passed their SOC 2 audit in half the expected time. **🔬 Research lab** — A research team runs 500+ short-lived Quilt agents on a K8s cluster. They use `quilt-base:scratch` for the smallest possible image, so the cluster can schedule 10× more agents per node. ## ✦ Try it right now ```bash # Pull the Alpine variant docker pull ghcr.io/superinstance/quilt-base:alpine # Run a Quilt agent on it docker run -it --rm ghcr.io/superinstance/quilt-base:alpine sh -c 'echo "Hello from quilt-base"' ``` Or browse the [live image registry on GitHub Container Registry](https://github.com/orgs/SuperInstance/packages). ## ✦ How it fits in the ecosystem `quilt-base` is the **foundation layer** of the Quilt 25-repo platform. The other infrastructure repos build on it: ``` quilt-base (this repo) ↑ ├── quilt-agent (agents that run on this base) ├── quilt-elf (Cloudflare Workers — uses a stripped-down variant) ├── quilt-pincher (reflex engine — runs on this base in 3 modes) ├── quilt-fleet (orchestrator that deploys images based on this base) ├── quilt-k3s (chaos tests run agents in containers from this base) ├── quilt-nomad (Nomad jobs use this base as their image) └── quilt-swarm (Swarm services use this base) ``` When you `docker run` a Quilt agent, this is the image. When you deploy to the edge, this is the image. When the elves run invisibly in the background, this is what they're running on. ## ✦ Why you should care If you've ever debugged a "works on my machine" issue at 2am. If you've ever had a security advisory tell you to update 200 packages in a 1.2GB image. If you've ever wondered why your production image is 4× bigger than it needs to be. If you've ever had a regulator ask you to prove your software supply chain is clean. This repo is for you. ## ✦ License Apache 2.0. See [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

The `quilt-base` project provides long-term support (LTS) for the most recent
major and minor release of every image variant. Older versions receive
critical security backports on a best-effort basis only.

| Variant    | Latest tag              | Supported           | EOL (planned) |
| ---------- | ----------------------- | ------------------- | ------------- |
| Alpine     | `alpine-latest`         | ✅ Yes              | T+12 months   |
| Ubuntu     | `ubuntu-latest`         | ✅ Yes              | T+24 months (Ubuntu LTS) |
| Distroless | `distroless-latest`     | ✅ Yes              | T+12 months   |
| Scratch    | `scratch-latest`        | ✅ Yes              | T+12 months   |

Where `T` is the date of the most recent LTS release for the upstream base
(Alpine 3.x, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, distroless Debian 12).

A version is considered **supported** when it:
1. Receives weekly Dependabot and Trivy scans.
2. Is rebuilt by the auto-rebuild workflow within 7 days of an upstream
   patch release.
3. Has a non-EOL SBOM published as a GitHub release asset.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

**Please do not file public GitHub issues for security vulnerabilities.**

Use GitHub's private vulnerability disclosure:
👉 https://github.com/SuperInstance/quilt-base/security/advisories/new

If you cannot use the GitHub UI (e.g. the advisory is embargoed or the
issue is in a private mirror), email `security@superinstance.dev` with
the subject line `quilt-base vulnerability report`. The PGP fingerprint
for this address is published on
<https://github.com/SuperInstance/quilt-base/blob/main/SECURITY.md>.

### What to include

- The variant (`alpine`, `ubuntu`, `distroless`, `scratch`) and tag
  (e.g. `alpine-0.1.0`).
- A reproducer: `docker run ...` command or a minimal Dockerfile.
- The exact CVE ID, if one is published.
- Whether the vulnerability is in the base image itself or in a
  downstream Quilt agent that uses it.

### Response targets

| Severity | Initial response | Patch target   |
| -------- | ---------------- | -------------- |
| CRITICAL | ≤ 24 hours       | ≤ 72 hours     |
| HIGH     | ≤ 3 business days| ≤ 14 days      |
| MEDIUM   | ≤ 7 business days| ≤ 30 days      |
| LOW      | ≤ 30 days        | next quarterly |

"Initial response" means an acknowledgement that the report was received
and a preliminary assessment of severity.

"Patch target" means a new image tag published to GHCR. We aim to backport
to all supported LTS branches simultaneously.

## Security Architecture

`quilt-base` images are hardened in the following ways. This is a summary;
the actual controls are encoded in the Dockerfiles under `/docker` and the
scan scripts under `/security`.

### Defense in depth

1. **No setuid binaries.** All setuid bits are stripped in the final
   image. Even if a non-root attacker exploits a busybox applet, they
   cannot escalate to root.

2. **No package manager in the final image.** `apk`, `apt`, and `dpkg`
   are removed from the Alpine and Ubuntu variants at build time. There
   is nothing to use to install further packages at runtime.

3. **No shell in the distroless / scratch variants.** The published
   images have no `/bin/sh`, no `bash`, no `ash`. `docker exec` will
   fail unless the downstream agent adds a debug binary.

4. **Non-root default user.** The Alpine and Ubuntu images run as UID
   1000 (`quilt`) by default. The distroless image uses UID 65532
   (`nonroot`).

5. **Pinned CA bundle.** Each image has a `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`
   that is the only CA bundle in the image. There is no fallback to
   `/etc/pki/tls` or `/usr/local/share/certs`.

6. **OCI labels.** Every image carries the standard
   `org.opencontainers.image.*` labels (creator, source, revision, etc.)
   so the supply chain is traceable.

7. **SBOMs.** Every release is published with both SPDX 2.3 and
   CycloneDX 1.5 SBOMs. They are available as workflow artifacts and as
   in-toto attestations via `cosign verify-attestation`.

### Continuous scanning

| Tool    | Frequency  | Failure mode                      |
| ------- | ---------- | --------------------------------- |
| Trivy   | Daily      | Opens a tracking issue + rebuilds |
| Grype   | Daily      | Posts to SARIF (best-effort)      |
| Dependabot | Weekly | Opens PR for upstream bumps       |
| Auto-rebuild | Weekly | Rolls forward to latest upstream  |

The full pipeline is in `.github/workflows/cve-scan.yml` and
`scripts/auto-rebuild.yml`.

### Known limitations

- **Alpine uses musl libc.** Some Node.js native modules (e.g.
  `bcrypt`) that depend on glibc semantics may not work. Use
  `quilt-base:ubuntu` for those.
- **Distroless has no shell.** Debugging requires a separate debug image
  (`gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:debug`) or a `kubectl debug`
  session.
- **Scratch has no OS at all.** Your binary MUST be statically linked
  with musl (Rust: `--target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, Go:
  `CGO_ENABLED=0`, C: `-static`).

## Acknowledgements

Vulnerability reporters who follow this policy are credited (with their
permission) in the corresponding GitHub Security Advisory. Reporters
who find a CRITICAL or HIGH issue that is patched within the target SLA
are listed in the project's `CREDITS.md` and offered a Quilt t-shirt.

## Policy version

This policy is version `1.0.0` and is reviewed annually. Changes are
tracked in `SECURITY.md`'s git history.
quilt-base-main/scripts/build-all.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Quilt Base — Build all variants and push to GHCR
# =============================================================================
# Builds every Quilt base image variant in parallel, tags each with
#   - the version (from `git describe --tags` or QUILT_BASE_VERSION env)
#   - the date (YYYY-MM-DD)
#   - the git SHA
#   - "latest" (only for the most recent successful build)
# then scans each with Trivy and Grype, and pushes to GitHub Container
# Registry (GHCR) at ghcr.io/SuperInstance/quilt-base.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build-all.sh [variant]  — build only one variant
#   scripts/build-all.sh            — build all
#   scripts/build-all.sh --no-push  — build & scan, but do not push
#   scripts/build-all.sh --no-scan  — build & push, skip CVE scan
#
# Environment:
#   GITHUB_REPOSITORY       — used to derive GHCR org (default: SuperInstance/quilt-base)
#   GITHUB_TOKEN            — GHCR auth token; required for push
#   QUILT_BASE_VERSION      — version tag (default: derived from git)
#   QUILT_PUSH              — "true" to push, anything else to skip (default: true)
#   BUILDX_BUILDER          — name of an existing buildx builder (optional)
#   PLATFORMS               — comma list (default: linux/amd64,linux/arm64)
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Strict mode
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
set -Eeuo pipefail
IFS=$'\n\t'
umask 022

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

GITHUB_REPOSITORY="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-SuperInstance/quilt-base}"
GHCR_REGISTRY="ghcr.io"
IMAGE_BASE="${GHCR_REGISTRY}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY,,}"
QUILT_PUSH="${QUILT_PUSH:-true}"
QUILT_SCAN="${QUILT_SCAN:-true}"
PLATFORMS="${PLATFORMS:-linux/amd64,linux/arm64}"
ONLY_VARIANT=""
USE_BUILDX_CACHE="${USE_BUILDX_CACHE:-true}"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variants — keep in lockstep with /docker/Dockerfile.* filenames.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
VARIANTS=(alpine ubuntu distroless scratch)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Logging
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
log()  { printf '[build-all] %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
fail() { printf '[build-all] ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Argument parsing
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --no-push)            QUILT_PUSH="false"; shift ;;
    --no-scan)            QUILT_SCAN="false"; shift ;;
    --variant)            ONLY_VARIANT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --platforms)          PLATFORMS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --no-buildkit-cache)  USE_BUILDX_CACHE="false"; shift ;;
    -h|--help)
      sed -n '2,30p' "$0"
      exit 0
      ;;
    *)
      # First positional = variant name
      if [[ -z "${ONLY_VARIANT}" ]] && [[ " ${VARIANTS[*]} " == *" $1 "* ]]; then
        ONLY_VARIANT="$1"
        shift
      else
        fail "unknown argument: $1"
      fi
      ;;
  esac
done

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Version resolution — git describe, with a sane fallback.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
resolve_version() {
  if [[ -n "${QUILT_BASE_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    printf '%s' "${QUILT_BASE_VERSION}"
    return
  fi
  if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -d "${REPO_ROOT}/.git" ]]; then
    git -C "${REPO_ROOT}" describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null \
      || git -C "${REPO_ROOT}" rev-parse --short HEAD
  else
    printf '0.1.0'
  fi
}

VERSION="$(resolve_version)"
DATE_TAG="$(date -u +%Y%m%d)"
GIT_SHA="$(git -C "${REPO_ROOT}" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"

log "version=${VERSION}  date=${DATE_TAG}  sha=${GIT_SHA}"
log "image base: ${IMAGE_BASE}"
log "platforms:  ${PLATFORMS}"
log "push:       ${QUILT_PUSH}"
log "scan:       ${QUILT_SCAN}"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# buildx setup — use a persistent builder for cache reuse.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
BUILDER_NAME="${BUILDX_BUILDER:-quilt-base-builder}"
if [[ "${USE_BUILDX_CACHE}" == "true" ]]; then
  if ! docker buildx inspect "${BUILDER_NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "creating buildx builder ${BUILDER_NAME}"
    docker buildx create \
      --name "${BUILDER_NAME}" \
      --driver docker-container \
      --bootstrap \
      --platform "${PLATFORMS}" >/dev/null
  fi
  docker buildx use "${BUILDER_NAME}"
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GHCR login — only required for push, but cheap to attempt.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "${QUILT_PUSH}" == "true" ]]; then
  if [[ -z "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]] && [[ -z "${GHCR_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
    fail "GITHUB_TOKEN (or GHCR_TOKEN) is required for push; set it in the environment"
  fi
  printf '%s' "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-${GHCR_TOKEN}}" \
    | docker login "${GHCR_REGISTRY}" -u "${GITHUB_ACTOR:-SuperInstance}" --password-stdin
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build a single variant. Emits the list of tags it pushed to stdout.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_variant() {
  local variant="$1"
  local dockerfile="${REPO_ROOT}/docker/Dockerfile.${variant}"

  if [[ ! -f "${dockerfile}" ]]; then
    log "SKIP ${variant}: no Dockerfile at ${dockerfile}"
    return 0
  fi

  log "=== building variant: ${variant} ==="

  local tags=(
    --tag "${IMAGE_BASE}:${variant}-${VERSION}"
    --tag "${IMAGE_BASE}:${variant}-${DATE_TAG}"
    --tag "${IMAGE_BASE}:${variant}-${GIT_SHA}"
  )
  if [[ "${variant}" == "alpine" ]]; then
    # The Alpine image is the "default" Quilt base, so it also gets the
    # untagged latest tag and the bare :VERSION tag.
    tags+=(
      --tag "${IMAGE_BASE}:latest"
      --tag "${IMAGE_BASE}:${VERSION}"
    )
  fi

  local cache_args=()
  if [[ "${USE_BUILDX_CACHE}" == "true" ]]; then
    cache_args+=(
      --cache-from "type=registry,ref=${IMAGE_BASE}:buildcache-${variant}"
      --cache-to   "type=registry,ref=${IMAGE_BASE}:buildcache-${variant},mode=max"
    )
  fi

  local build_args=(
    --platform "${PLATFORMS}"
    --file "${dockerfile}"
    --label "io.quilt.base.build_date=${DATE_TAG}"
    --label "io.quilt.base.vcs_ref=${GIT_SHA}"
    --label "io.quilt.base.version=${VERSION}"
    --build-arg "QUILT_BASE_VERSION=${VERSION}"
    --build-arg "BUILD_DATE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
    --build-arg "VCS_REF=${GIT_SHA}"
    --build-arg "VCS_URL=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
  )

  if [[ "${QUILT_PUSH}" == "true" ]]; then
    build_args+=(--push)
  else
    build_args+=(--load)
  fi

  docker buildx build "${build_args[@]}" "${cache_args[@]}" "${tags[@]}" "${REPO_ROOT}"
  printf '%s\n' "${IMAGE_BASE}:${variant}-${VERSION}"
}

export -f build_variant log
export IMAGE_BASE DATE_TAG GIT_SHA PLATFORMS QUILT_PUSH REPO_ROOT GITHUB_REPOSITORY USE_BUILDX_CACHE

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parallel build — one variant per CPU, max 4 at once.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ -n "${ONLY_VARIANT}" ]]; then
  BUILT="$(build_variant "${ONLY_VARIANT}")"
  BUILT_VARIANTS=("${ONLY_VARIANT}")
else
  log "building ${#VARIANTS[@]} variants in parallel"
  # xargs is portable; -P limits concurrency; -I{} passes variant name.
  BUILT="$(printf '%s\n' "${VARIANTS[@]}" \
    | xargs -n 1 -P 4 -I {} bash -c 'build_variant "$@"' _ {})"
  BUILT_VARIANTS=("${VARIANTS[@]}")
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CVE scan each built image. We use the `variant-VERSION` tag (the
# immutable one) so reruns are reproducible.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "${QUILT_SCAN}" == "true" ]]; then
  log "=== running CVE scan on each built image ==="
  SCAN_FAILED=()
  for variant in "${BUILT_VARIANTS[@]}"; do
    local_tag="${IMAGE_BASE}:${variant}-${VERSION}"
    log "scanning ${local_tag}"
    if ! "${REPO_ROOT}/security/trivy-scan.sh" "${local_tag}"; then
      SCAN_FAILED+=("${local_tag}")
    fi
    # Grype is best-effort; if it's not installed, do not fail the build.
    if command -v grype >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      "${REPO_ROOT}/security/grype-scan.sh" "${local_tag}" || true
    fi
  done
  if [[ ${#SCAN_FAILED[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    fail "CVE scan FAILED for: ${SCAN_FAILED[*]}"
  fi
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SBOM generation for each variant.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ -f "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/sbom-generate.sh" ]]; then
  log "=== generating SBOMs ==="
  for variant in "${BUILT_VARIANTS[@]}"; do
    "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/sbom-generate.sh" "${IMAGE_BASE}:${variant}-${VERSION}" || true
  done
fi

log "=== DONE ==="
printf '%s\n' "${BUILT}"
